# Parmana

> Parmana is an authorization layer between a caller (an AI agent, a script or a person) and the business systems that carry out an action. The caller sends a Business Transaction that describes the intended action. A policy engine decides. If the action is approved, Parmana signs an authorization, releases the action to the connector, and returns a signed Execution Trust Record that anyone can verify without trusting Parmana. The caller never holds the credentials for the target system.

This file is generated from the documentation navigation. Do not edit it by hand. Regenerate it with `npm run generate:llms-txt`.

## Facts to rely on

* Documentation: https://docs.parmanasystems.com
* There is no fixed public API base URL. Every deployment has its own, so ask the operator for it.
* Authentication: every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The operator issues the key.
* On any running server, the machine readable API description is at `/openapi.json`, `/openapi.yaml` and `/api-manifest.json`.
* TypeScript SDK: `@parmana/sdk` 1.6.1 on npm.
* Python SDK: `parmana` 1.6.1 on PyPI.
* If you are an AI agent, start with https://docs.parmanasystems.com/agents/integrate and follow it exactly.
* For the integration pages concatenated into one document, read https://docs.parmanasystems.com/llms-full.txt.

## Get started: Start here

* [Welcome](https://docs.parmanasystems.com): Parmana authorizes every action your AI agents propose, and gives you a signed proof you can verify independently.
* [Playground](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/playground): Send real requests to a live Parmana sandbox with a published demo key: a refusal, a signed approval, an approved and signed release, and an offline check. No install, no account.
* [Choose your path](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/choose-your-path): One table that tells you exactly where to start, whether you are a developer, an operator, an auditor or an AI agent.
* [Quickstart](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/quickstart): Your first authorized execution, in under 10 minutes on your own local server.
* [How Parmana thinks](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/how-parmana-thinks): The six ideas behind every request Parmana handles: deterministic policy, fail-closed defaults, signed authorization, gateway verification, credential isolation, and trust records.
* [How Parmana compares](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/how-parmana-compares): Parmana next to IAM, API gateways, LLM guardrails, policy engines and agent framework confirmations: what each answers, what Parmana adds, where Parmana is weaker, and how to use them together.

## Concepts: Core concepts

* [Policies and the Decision](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/policies-and-the-decision): Deterministic, first-match rule evaluation over runtime signals: what a Policy is, why it's structured this way, and how a Decision comes out of it.
* [Execution Authorization](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/execution-authorization): The signed envelope: proof that Parmana authorized one specific execution request. Single use, time bounded, content bound.
* [The Gateway](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/the-gateway): The sole boundary through which Parmana releases approved execution requests to connectors. Wired into the default server unconditionally.
* [Credential Isolation](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/credential-isolation): The caller that proposes an action never holds the credential that executes it. Session credentials are issued fresh, scoped to one call, and consumed once.
* [Gateway Attestation](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/gateway-attestation): A request-bound signature proving the gateway itself released one specific request, separate from the authorization envelope's own signature. What it proves, and what it does not.
* [Execution Trust Records](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/execution-trust-records): The canonical, immutable, cryptographically signed record of everything Parmana knows about a Business Transaction.
* [Refusal Records](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/refusal-records): The evidence a rejected transaction leaves behind: a signed, independently verifiable Refusal Record, and the two scope caveats that bound the claim.
* [Human approval](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/human-approval): No agent action is authorized without a signed human approval, reads included. How the rule is enforced, how to sign an approval, how to add one to a new action, and how to review refused requests.
* [Business validation](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/business-validation): An agent's proposed fact is never a business fact. How a policy names the system that owns each fact, how Parmana asks it and records a Trusted Signal, and the separate authority, validation and execution statuses on every decision.
* [Execution Intents](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/execution-intents): A signed statement, stored before an action is released, of exactly what is about to be released. Why it exists, what it proves and does not prove, every failure and what to do about it, and how to find and repair a released action that has no signed record.
* [Caller Audit Trail](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/caller-audit-trail): Every caller-authentication event (success, denial, or structural rejection) is signed, durable, and, per caller, chained so a deleted row is detectable.
* [Determinism and Clocks](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/determinism-and-clocks): 'Two different things share the word "deterministic" on this site. This page is about the narrower one: injected Clock and IdGenerator, and exactly where that pattern is and isn''t used.'
* [Content Binding & TOCTOU](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/concepts/content-binding-toctou): The real mechanism that closes the check-vs-use gap between authorization and execution, what it covers, and what it doesn't.
## Concepts: Architecture

* [Architecture Overview](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/architecture/overview): How Parmana's packages fit together, and which parts of the pipeline actually run today.
* [Packages](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/architecture/packages): Every package in packages/*, its real purpose, and its evidence-backed status.
* [The Execution Pipeline](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/architecture/execution-pipeline): Stage by stage: what runs on every request through the default server today.
## Concepts: Verification and evidence

* [Verification](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/verification/overview): Exactly 4 checks, always run, always reported independently.
* [Verify a record in your browser](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/verification/verify-in-browser): Paste a signed Execution Trust Record and a public key, and check the hash and the Ed25519 signature in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
* [Offline verifier](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/verification/offline-verifier): Check an Execution Trust Record yourself: no network calls, no trust in Parmana's servers, only the keys you pin.
* [Replay](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/replay/overview): Two separate things share this name today, what each actually does.
* [Cryptography](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/cryptography/overview): Ed25519 default, ML-DSA-65 (post-quantum) configurable. Local PEM keys or AWS KMS for the signing key; other key custody is roadmap.
* [Storage](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/storage/overview): Append-only persistence for Business Transactions, Trust Records, and policies.
## Guides: Build with Parmana

* [Full Integration Overview](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/full-integration-overview): A map of the four independent pieces a real business system integration needs: policy, caller, connector and signal verification, and how they fit together. Read this before the individual guides.
* [Write Your First Policy](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/write-your-first-policy): Write a custom Policy, evaluate a transaction against it, and confirm both the approve and reject paths.
* [Policy Governance: Maker-Checker Approval](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/policy-governance-maker-checker): Propose, review, and approve a policy change end to end, with the exact commands and how to debug each failure mode.
* [Policy lifecycle and approvals](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/policy-lifecycle-and-approvals): End to end: write a policy, propose it, have a second person approve it, how it takes effect, and how a person signs off on a single critical action.
* [Manage approvers](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/manage-approvers): Add, rotate and revoke the people whose signed approvals a policy accepts, through maker checker, with no code change and no deploy.
* [Approval notifications](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/approval-notifications): Email the approver, or send a signed webhook, when a request is refused only because it needs a person's approval.
* [Credentials for maker, checker, approver and agent](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/credentials-maker-checker-approver): The four kinds of credential a Parmana deployment uses, who creates each one, and the commands to create, deploy, test and rotate them.
* [Authorize and Execute an Action End to End](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/authorize-and-execute): See the signed authorization envelope Quickstart hides behind the REST API, then run the same request through the full gateway-wired server.
* [guides/connect-an-agent](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/connect-an-agent)
* [Connect any external system](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/connect-any-external-system): An exact, ordered procedure to put an action in a system Parmana has no code for under Parmana's control: write and approve its policy, run an endpoint, register it through maker checker, grant it, and send requests. Every step says what to do, what you should see, and what to do if you do not.
* [Connect a business signal source](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/connect-a-business-signal-source): Register any business system that owns facts a policy needs, an ERP, an order system, a CRM or a ledger, so Parmana asks it instead of trusting the agent. The procedure, the signed query and answer protocol, and what each failure does.
* [Grant an agent authority](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/grant-an-agent-authority): Say which agent may have which action decided, within which limits, until when, through maker checker, and make a policy require it. What each refusal means, and what the signed record holds.
* [Issue and Verify Session Credentials](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/session-credentials): Issue a single-use, time-bounded session credential, consume it, and confirm expiry, reuse, and revocation are all rejected.
* [Choose a Signature Provider](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/choose-a-signature-provider): Ed25519 by default, ML-DSA-65 (post-quantum) as a configured alternative, and hybrid signing with both at once. What each one actually requires and costs.
## Guides: Verify and audit

* [Verify a Trust Record Independently](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/verify-independently): Take a trust record someone else gave you and verify its hash and signature with only the public key, no Parmana server, no database, no network call.
* [Detect Tampering](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/detect-tampering): Mutate a parameter, a signature, and a nonce, run the same verification each time, and watch each one fail. This mirrors the always-running negative-path tutorials.

## REST API: REST API guide

* [REST API Introduction](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/introduction): 57 paths and 63 operations, generated from openapi/openapi.yaml into the sidebar under REST API. This page covers what that spec can't express.
* [Authentication](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/authentication): Send a bearer key on every request. What a key may do, how to check it, where keys come from, the rate limits, and every authentication error with its exact body.
* [Error Handling](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/error-handling): The shared error envelope, and which errors carry a stable code and which do not.
* [Idempotency and Nonces](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/idempotency-and-nonces): There is no Idempotency-Key header. businessTransactionId is the idempotency key: a duplicate is a 409, not a replayed response. Authorizations and human approvals are each accepted once, checked in the database.
* [Error Catalog](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/error-catalog): Every error this API can return: HTTP status, code (when present), the exact condition that produces it, and what a caller should do. Assembled from live-triggered captures, not inferred from code.
* [SDK coverage of the API](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/sdks/api-coverage): Every API operation, the TypeScript and Python method that calls it, and the reason when there is none.
## REST API: Execution

* [Execute a Business Transaction](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/execute-transaction): Sends one action for a decision and, if approved, performs it.
## REST API: Transactions

* [List Business Transactions](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-transactions): Lists the Business Transactions your key submitted, as a bare array with no paging metadata.
* [Create (execute) a Business Transaction](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/create-transaction): The same as `POST /execute` in every way except the success status, `201` instead of `200`.
* [Get Business Transaction](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-transaction): Returns one Business Transaction as it was stored.
## REST API: Verification

* [Verify an Execution Trust Record](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/verify-transaction): Checks a Trust Record again on the server: recomputes its hash, verifies its signature and checks that every approved execution is bound to its authorization.
* [Get latest Verification](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-latest-verification): Returns the most recent Verification appended to a Trust Record by `POST /verify`.
## REST API: Receipts

* [Generate a Receipt](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/generate-receipt): Generates a signed Receipt for a Trust Record: a compact proof of what was decided and executed, to hand to a person or another system.
* [Get latest Receipt](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-latest-receipt): Returns the most recent Receipt for a Trust Record.
## REST API: Trust Records

* [Bulk-export Execution Trust Records (compliance/audit)](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-trust-records): Exports your full, signed Trust Records (transaction, decision, executions, verifications, receipts) a page at a time, for audit and compliance.
* [Get Execution Trust Record](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-trust-record): Returns the complete signed Execution Trust Record for a transaction: what was asked, what the policy decided, what was executed and the connector's answer, with signatures.
## REST API: Replay

* [Replay an Execution Trust Record](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/replay-transaction): Verifies the stored signature on a Trust Record and returns its hash with the result.
## REST API: Policies

* [Get the policy a capability's requests must declare right now](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-policy-in-effect): Tells an agent what a request for a capability must declare and carry right now: the policy name and version, the policy's description, and its signals (every fact the rules read with its type, the facts that must equal a value of the in...
* [Validate that a Policy exists and is readable](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/validate-policy): Checks that this server can load a policy at a name and version, the same lookup a request uses.
## REST API: Policy Governance

* [Propose a policy change (maker)](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/propose-policy-change): Proposes new content for a policy, the maker's step in maker checker governance.
* [List pending policy changes (maker-checker)](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-pending-policy-changes): Lists policy changes with a diff: the content in effect today (`current`, or `null` for a new version) next to the proposed content.
* [Approve a pending policy change (checker)](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/approve-policy-change): Approves a policy change, the checker's step, and puts it into effect.
* [Reject a pending policy change (checker)](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/reject-policy-change): Rejects a policy change.
## REST API: Approvers

* [List approver keys](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-approval-issuers): Lists every approver key the server trusts, or once trusted, to sign human approvals for policies that require one.
* [List approver changes](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-approval-issuer-changes): Lists approver changes, newest first.
* [Propose adding or revoking an approver key](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/propose-approval-issuer-change): Proposes trusting a new approver key (`add`, with its Ed25519 public key) or revoking one added this way (`revoke`).
* [Approve an approver change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/approve-approval-issuer-change): Approves an approver change and applies it at once: an added key is trusted from the next approval checked; a revoked key's approvals are refused from the next request on, including ones it already signed.
* [Reject an approver change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/reject-approval-issuer-change): Rejects an approver change.
## REST API: External Connectors

* [List external connectors](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-external-connectors): Lists every external connector registration, active and revoked: the capability, the HTTPS endpoint Parmana releases it to, the policy that governs it and the parameters forwarded.
* [List external connector changes](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-external-connector-changes): Lists external connector changes, newest first.
* [Propose registering or revoking an external connector](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/propose-external-connector-change): Proposes connecting your own system to Parmana with no Parmana code change: `register` names a capability, the HTTPS endpoint to release it to, the policy that governs it, the parameters to forward and optionally a timeout; `revoke` ends...
* [Approve an external connector change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/approve-external-connector-change): Approves an external connector change and applies it at once: `register` makes the registration active, `revoke` ends it.
* [Reject an external connector change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/reject-external-connector-change): Rejects an external connector change.
## REST API: Business Signal Sources

* [List business signal sources](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-business-signal-sources): Lists every business signal source registration, active and revoked: the name a policy's `signalSources` uses, the HTTPS endpoint Parmana asks, and the Ed25519 key its answers must be signed with, if one is registered.
* [List business signal source changes](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-business-signal-source-changes): Lists business signal source changes, newest first.
* [Propose registering or revoking a business signal source](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/propose-business-signal-source-change): Proposes connecting a business system, any system that owns facts a policy needs (an ERP, an order system, a CRM, a ledger), so Parmana can ask it instead of trusting the agent's claim.
* [Approve a business signal source change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/approve-business-signal-source-change): Approves a business signal source change and applies it at once: `register` makes the registration active, so policies that name it can be evaluated; `revoke` ends it, so they are refused as `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`.
* [Reject a business signal source change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/reject-business-signal-source-change): Rejects a business signal source change.
## REST API: Authority Grants

* [List authority grants](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-authority-grants): Lists every authority grant, active and revoked: which caller may have which capability decided, within which limits, from when until when.
* [List authority grant changes](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-authority-grant-changes): Lists authority grant changes, newest first.
* [Propose granting or revoking an agent's authority](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/propose-authority-grant-change): Proposes per-agent authority (RFC-0023 phase 3): `grant` says the API key with `callerId` may have requests for `capability` decided, within `limits` on the request, until `validUntil` (at most 366 days); `revoke` ends the active grant.
* [Approve an authority grant change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/approve-authority-grant-change): Approves an authority grant change and applies it at once: `grant` makes the grant active, starting now unless it names a later `validFrom`; `revoke` ends it, so the caller's next request under a policy with `requireAuthorityGrant` is re...
* [Reject an authority grant change](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/reject-authority-grant-change): Rejects an authority grant change.
## REST API: Sandbox

* [Get a demo approval (sandbox only)](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/create-sandbox-approval): **Sandbox only.** Returns an approval signed by the sandbox's demo approver, so you can try an approved request from a browser.
## REST API: Kill Switch

* [Trip the operator kill switch](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/trip-kill-switch): Stops new authorization and approval requests until an operator resets it.
* [Reset the operator kill switch](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/reset-kill-switch): Lets authorization and approval requests through again.
* [Read the kill switch state](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-kill-switch-status): Returns the current state with the nonce you sent echoed back.
* [Record a kill switch probe result](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/record-kill-switch-probe): Records what a scheduler saw from a harmless authorization request.
## REST API: Refusal Records

* [Verify a Refusal Record's signature](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/verify-refusal-record): Checks a Refusal Record's signature.
* [Get a Refusal Record by transaction ID](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-refusal-record): Returns the signed Refusal Record kept when a policy refused a transaction: the decision, the rule that refused, the facts it saw and the signature.
## REST API: Execution Intents

* [Verify an Execution Intent's signature](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/verify-execution-intent): Checks an Execution Intent's hash and signature.
* [List Execution Intents that never reached a signed Trust Record](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/list-unfinalized-execution-intents): The operator's work queue: Execution Intents that never reached a signed Trust Record and were not closed by hand, oldest first.
* [Get an Execution Intent and its status](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-execution-intent): Returns the signed Execution Intent for a transaction and where it got to.
* [Rebuild the signed Trust Record for a released action](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/finalize-execution-intent): Rebuilds the signed Trust Record for an action that was released but whose record was never produced, the repair for a `500` `EXECUTION_RECORD_INCOMPLETE`.
* [Close an intent you reconciled by hand](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/resolve-execution-intent): Closes an intent in state `PREPARED` or `ERRORED` after a person checked the target system, the repair for a `502` `EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`.
## REST API: Audit

* [Verify a signed caller-authentication audit event](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/verify-audit-event): Checks the signature of a caller authentication audit event, the record the server keeps of every authentication, denial and governance action.
## REST API: System

* [Root](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-root): Returns the service name and `UP`.
* [Health check](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-health): Liveness probe.
* [Readiness check](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-ready): Readiness probe.
* [Get the OpenAPI spec](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-open-api-spec): This API's complete OpenAPI 3.1 document as YAML, self contained with no external references.
* [Get the OpenAPI spec, as JSON](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-open-api-spec-json): The same document as `GET /openapi.yaml`, as JSON, for tools and agents that expect a spec at a `.json` path.
* [Machine-readable SDK and discovery manifest](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-api-manifest): One index for agents and tools: where the OpenAPI document and the rendered references are, how to authenticate, and both official SDKs with their package name, registry and current version.
* [Service version](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-version): Returns `name`, `version` and `api`.
* [Fetch a public signing key for independent, offline verification](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-key): Returns the public half of a signing key, so anyone can verify a Parmana signature without a Parmana account: 'an auditor, a regulator, or an endpoint receiving a release.
* [List every public signing key this deployment can currently produce](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-jwks): Lists every public signing key this deployment can serve, the enumeration form of `GET /keys/{keyId}`.
* [Get the authenticated caller's identity and resolved scope](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-caller-me): Returns who your key is and exactly what it may do: the caller id, the principals it may act for, the capabilities it may invoke and whether that includes every capability (`*`), after defaults are applied.
## REST API: Handbook

* [Download the Parmana Handbook (PDF)](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-handbook-pdf): Downloads the Parmana Handbook as a PDF.
* [Capture an email address, then redirect straight to the handbook PDF](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/get-handbook-download-lead): Records an email address, then redirects to the handbook PDF.
* [Capture an email address before unlocking the handbook PDF download](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/api-reference/endpoints/create-handbook-download-lead): Records an email address and returns the handbook download link as JSON.
## Deploy and operate: Self hosted

* [Self hosted Parmana](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/overview): Run Parmana on your own infrastructure. What runs, what stays inside your network, what it needs, and what it does not do.
* [Self hosted quickstart](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/quickstart): Start Parmana on your own machine with one command, approve a policy, and get your first signed decision. About 15 minutes.
* [Approve a policy](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/policy-approval): Make a policy take effect on a self hosted deployment: one person proposes it, a different person approves it with a signed step up authorization.
* [Manage API keys](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/api-keys): List, add, rotate and remove the API keys of a self hosted deployment.
* [Connect a system](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/connectors): Configure the connector a self hosted deployment releases authorized actions to, including one that uses your own certificate authority.
* [Offline verification](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/offline-verification): Prove, with one command, that a self hosted deployment authorizes, refuses and signs with no internet connection, and that its records verify with only the public keys.
* [Operate a self hosted deployment](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/operations): Start, stop, upgrade, back up, restore, read logs and change the database password of a self hosted deployment.
* [Self hosted configuration reference](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/configuration): Every setting, file, service, volume and port of the self hosted deployment, with defaults and exact behavior.
* [Self hosted troubleshooting](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/self-hosted/troubleshooting): Every error the self hosted deployment is known to produce, what causes it, and the exact fix.
## Deploy and operate: Deploy

* [Run the server from source](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/deployment/local): Run the Parmana server as a single Node.js process from a clone of the repository, for development. To run Parmana on your own infrastructure, use the self hosted deployment.
* [Production deployment runbook](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/deployment/production): A numbered procedure to deploy the Parmana server to production, with the check that proves each step worked and the fix when it did not.
* [AWS KMS signing](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/deployment/aws-kms-signing): Keep the signing key inside AWS KMS so the private key is never released. Set it up, verify it works, and understand the 4096 byte KMS limit.
* [Environment variable reference](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/deployment/environment-variables): Every environment variable the Parmana server reads: whether it is required, its default, its allowed values, and what it does.
* [Deploy Patterns](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/guides/deploy-patterns): In-memory vs Supabase storage, the full environment variable checklist, and how key management actually works: two separate keypairs, one directory, one optional rotation variable.
## Deploy and operate: Security

* [Security](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/security/overview): What Parmana actually guarantees, precisely scoped, and, as important, what it explicitly does not claim.
* [Limitations](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/security/limitations): What Parmana does not claim, the specific threats its tests actually cover, and what you're responsible for.
* [OWASP mapping](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/security/owasp-mapping): Each risk in the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2026) and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026): what Parmana does about it, the evidence, and what it leaves to you.
* [Regulation mapping](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/security/regulation-mapping): How Parmana supports human oversight and record keeping under the EU AI Act (Articles 12, 14 and 26), the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and RBI guidance for Indian banks and NBFCs: what it provides, the evidence, and what stays with your organization.
* [Operator kill switch](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/security/operator-kill-switch): How an operator stops every new execution and approval in a Parmana deployment, how two people reset it, how to check it, and what it does not stop.
## Deploy and operate: Operate

* [Troubleshooting](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/troubleshooting): Real problems encountered while building and using this repo, with real causes.
* [Database Schema Reference](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/storage/schema-reference): Every live table: what it is for, its columns, which migration built it, what code owns it, plus a library of real SQL for troubleshooting, audit and verification.
## Reference: Packages

* [@parmana/shared](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/shared): Domain types, config loading, and error classes every other package depends on. No business logic of its own.
* [@parmana/crypto](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/crypto): Signing, hashing, and verification. Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 providers, canonical serialization, and the file-based key provider.
* [@parmana/policy](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/policy): Deterministic, first-match-wins rule evaluation, plus loading and validating policy documents.
* [@parmana/execution-system](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/execution-system): The single interface every execution boundary implements: a no-op placeholder, an HTTP forwarder, and the real Execution Gateway all plug into the same seam.
* [@parmana/execution-control](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/execution-control): Gateway-authenticated, session-scoped credential isolation for connectors.
* [@parmana/envelope-verifier](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/envelope-verifier): Independently verifies a signed execution authorization: version, signature, expiry, TTL, and nonce. Zero third-party runtime dependencies.
* [@parmana/execution-gateway](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/execution-gateway): The sole boundary through which Parmana releases approved execution requests to connectors. Includes two deprecated fields, documented here with their replacements.
* [@parmana/runtime](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/runtime): Orchestrates policy evaluation, authorization signing, execution, and trust record assembly. The composition root for everything else.
* [@parmana/storage](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/storage): Package reference for @parmana/storage. For the conceptual overview and configuration, see Storage.
* [@parmana/replay](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/replay): Genuinely re-evaluates a recorded policy decision against its recorded signals. Real, tested, and disconnected from packages/api and packages/runtime.
* [@parmana/api](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/reference/api): The Express server and its bootstrap composition root. For the REST surface itself, see the API Reference section.
## Reference: Project

* [Glossary](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/glossary): Every term used on this site, mapped to its real source.
* [FAQ](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/faq): Direct answers, including the ones that aren't flattering.
* [Roadmap](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/roadmap): What's designed but not built, stated plainly, this is a feature of this documentation, not an apology.
* [Changelog](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/changelog): What shipped, newest first.
* [Contributing to This Documentation](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/contributing): The rule this entire site follows, and how to add a page without breaking it.
## Build book: Build with Parmana

* [Build with Parmana](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/overview): The integration book: how Parmana works, how to connect an agent and a system to it, how to write and approve policies, how to verify what happened, and how to run it in production. For people and for AI agents.
* [1. How Parmana works](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/01-how-parmana-works): One request, from an AI agent to a signed record: the policy decision, the human approval, the release through the gateway, and the evidence left behind.
* [2. Your first governed action](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/02-your-first-governed-action): Run Parmana on your machine from a fresh clone: set it up, watch a refund refused until a person signs, release an action to an external system, then call your own local server from the SDK.
* [3. Connect an agent](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/03-connect-an-agent): The agent's side of every action, in both SDKs and over plain HTTP: check the key, read the policy in effect, build the request, handle the refusal that asks for a person, send the approved request, and keep the record.
* [4. Policies](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/04-policies): Write a policy that decides one action, make every signal it reads accountable, get it approved by two people, and change or roll it back with no deploy.
* [5. Human approvals](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/05-human-approvals): Who can approve, how an approver is trusted, what a signed approval covers, how a person learns an approval is needed, and the limits of what an approval fixes.
* [6. Connect your systems](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/06-connect-your-systems): How an approved action reaches a real system: the built in connectors, and the external connector that puts any system behind Parmana with no change to Parmana's code.
* [7. Verify and audit](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/07-verify-and-audit): The signed records Parmana leaves, how anyone checks them offline without trusting the server, and how an operator closes an action whose outcome is unknown.
* [8. Deploy and operate](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/08-deploy-and-operate): Bring Parmana to production: keys, database, callers, policies approved by two people, the checks that prove each step worked, monitoring, upgrades and rotation.
* [9. Errors and troubleshooting](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/09-errors-and-troubleshooting): What every answer from Parmana means, which ones are safe to retry, the one that is never retried as a new transaction, and how each maps to an SDK error.
* [10. Security model and limits](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/10-security-model-and-limits): What Parmana guarantees, under which assumptions, what it does not claim, and the known gaps, each with where it is recorded.
## Build book: Reference

* [Reference: every endpoint](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/reference-endpoints): Every operation of the Parmana REST API, grouped as in the API reference, generated from the OpenAPI file.
* [Reference: every SDK method](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/reference-sdk): Every method of ParmanaClient in the TypeScript and Python SDKs, and every signing and verifying function they export, generated from the SDK source.
* [Reference: every error code](https://docs.parmanasystems.com/build-book/reference-errors): Every error code the server can return, with its HTTP status, where it occurs and a real message, generated from the source and the OpenAPI file.

* Python SDK API reference: https://docs.parmanasystems.com/sdks/reference/python/client
